answer: Stop sybils with a zephyr census, a thread of peer proof, and hollow decoy slots. Each identity must weave one thread through distinct peer attestations, and its bond grows with each peer the thread shares with another identity. A zephyr audit pulls a random thread: when a second thread claims the same peer set as an earlier thread, both bonds slash together, so N clones lose about N squared bonds while a lone identity risks one. A clone that passes through a hollow slot is exposed, and its whole cluster forfeits its bond, so faking scale destroys the very capital it needs to look real.
